brief:
The S&P 500 rose 0.19% to 7718.55, driven by strong earnings growth, while the Nasdaq rose 0.21% on a tech rally, despite rising bond yields.

S&P 500 (+0.19% to 7718.55): S&P 500 Earnings Growth Boost. The S&P 500 rose 0.19% to 7718.55 as investors focused on strong earnings growth, which underpinned the market, despite rising bond yields. [1] This move suggests traders are watching the impact of improving economic data on corporate profits. [4]
Nasdaq (+0.21% to 26997.01): Nasdaq Rises on Tech Rally. The Nasdaq rose as hedge funds increased bets on tech stocks, driven by the AI rally, [5]. This move suggests traders are optimistic about the sector's performance, [2]. However, a report from Yahoo Finance indicates that Nvidia's decline and rising Treasury yields may have pulled some investors out of tech stocks, [6].
10-Year Yield (+0.99% to 5.21): Treasury Yields Surge Amid Rate Hike Fears. The 10-year yield rose to its highest level since 2007, driven by concerns about the Federal Reserve's interest rate hike plans. Traders are watching the market's reaction to the Fed's signals, with some analysts suggesting that the jump in Treasury yields may be helping to stabilize the market. The 30-year Treasury yield also hit its highest level since 2004, adding to the market's volatility.
USD/JPY (-0.58% to 157.35): USD/JPY Falls Below 157 Yen. The USD/JPY pair fell below 157 yen after Japan's financial chief discussed financial ties with the US, sparking concerns about Japan's intervention in the currency market [11]. Traders are watching for any signs of yen intervention, which could impact the pair's movement [14]. The dollar's decline may be attributed to a decrease in oil prices, which led to a rally in the yen [12].
Crude Oil (-0.72% to 93.93): Oil Prices Take a Hit. Crude oil fell 0.72% to 93.93 as markets looked to an Iran truce, but remained wary of attacks on oil facilities [15]. This cautious approach was reflected in a jump in oil prices the previous day after Houthis fired missiles at Saudi facilities [16]. The decline in oil prices was also influenced by a decline in Eurozone bond yields and a stabilization of US Treasury yields [17]. Meanwhile, investors were seeking progress on US-Iran talks, which led to a rebound in oil prices [18].
Gold (+0.4% to 4315.0): Gold Prices Rise Despite Inflation Concerns. Gold prices rose 0.4% to 4315.0 despite concerns about inflation, as traders may be betting on a weaker US dollar and stronger demand from sovereign investors. [19] Reuters reported that mounting rate hike bets keep weekly loss in sight for gold, but Kitco's AM Report suggested that underlying demand is strengthening. [20] Yahoo Finance also noted that gold prices are battling support at $4,300, but [21] Kitco predicted that gold will hit $4,900/oz in 2026 on strong sovereign demand. [22] USA Today reported a 2.37% fall in gold prices on the previous day, but the current move suggests a reversal. No clear catalyst appeared in the news, but traders may be watching for signs of a weakening US dollar and strengthening demand from sovereign investors.
